key_facts: 11-year-old boy presented with a 7-year history of progressive skin hardening
Skin hardening is unilateral and involves the right thigh and buttock
Recent limitation of motion in the right limb joint
Normal results for routine blood tests, autoantibodies, immunoglobulins, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
MRI of the right thigh showed slight thickening of subcutaneous tissue and T2 signal abnormality
Histopathological findings included normal epidermis, mild pigmentation, and increased density of fibroblasts
Immunohistochemical staining showed increased expression of CD34 in the reticular dermis

raw.rationale: The patient's unilateral skin hardening, recent limitation of motion in the right limb joint, and histopathological findings of increased density of fibroblasts with normal epidermis are consistent with Segmental Stiff Skin Syndrome. The condition's segmental distribution and lack of systemic involvement or inflammation also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Stiff Skin Syndrome
rejected.why: Stiff Skin Syndrome typically presents with more widespread skin involvement and often has a more pronounced inflammatory component, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Linear Scleroderma
rejected.why: Linear Scleroderma usually presents with a more linear or band-like distribution of skin hardening, often with more significant inflammation and autoantibody positivity, which is not present in this case.
